title: Language Access at Migrant Health Centers: A Practical Guide
summary: Learn how migrant health centers can improve language access across indigenous and regional languages, mobile care, after-hours visits.
body_markdown:
###


Ask for the patient's preferred language for medical communication, not only country of origin or household language. Capture dialect when relevant, and ask whether the patient reads the same language they speak. This helps avoid treating every patient from a Spanish-speaking country as having the same language needs.


###


Written translation is not enough when a patient has limited literacy in the language they speak. Oral interpretation, visual explanation, and teach-back can be more useful for medication instructions, safety guidance, and follow-up plans.


###


Use a language-access option that can start immediately on the devices staff already carry. Opalite supports 150+ languages and dialects through AI, which is useful when a specific interpreter is not readily available at the time of the visit.


###


Store preferred language and interpreter need as structured data, document the interpreted encounter clearly, and make sure follow-up instructions are understandable across sites. Opalite can also draft multilingual clinical documentation from the encounter to help preserve context in the record.


###


Track time to active interpretation, less common language requests, use during outreach and after-hours care, staff workarounds, patient understanding, and whether language preference follows the patient across sites and follow-up calls.
